text:
infra-oncall: :rotating_light: Automated alert: multiple containers on gpunode-23 restarted 15x in 2m. egress 5xx spike. dmesg shows repeated kernel messages: 'GPU: illegal memory access at 0x7f8... (misaligned device address)'. tagging here.

ops-bot: Auto-incident created: INC-2026-0431. Paging pd-oncall. Notifying kernel-eng and infra-sre.

emma: seeing same on gpunode-21/23/24 across us-west-2. Most crashes are serving-runtime containers (ml-serve). Repro rate ~ 12%.

raj: quick triage: container logs show `cudaErrorIllegalAddress` immediately before crash. stack shows runtime allocator -> kernel launch -> device mem access. paste logs below.

raj: ```
E ml-serve: runtime: cuLaunchKernel failed: cudaErrorIllegalAddress
E ml-serve: stack: conv_kernel +0x1a3
E ml-serve: device ptr: 0x7f8a3b000
E kernel: [ 1352.412345] GPU: illegal memory access at address 0x7f8a3b000
```

sasha: can we cordon gpunode-23 and drain? want to stop further restarts.

emma: yes doing `kubectl cordon gpunode-23` and `kubectl drain gpunode-23 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` now.

ops-bot: gpunode-23 cordoned and draining. 6 pods evicted, 2 failed to reschedule due to GPU scheduling constraints.

kernel-eng: ping. attaching kernel oops trace from dmesg: ```
[ 1352.412345] GPU: unaligned address fault at 0x7f8a3b000, ip=0xffffffffa12b3c, sp=ffff8881234
[ 1352.412348] Call Trace:
[ 1352.412350]  gpu_copy+0x84/0xd0
[ 1352.412352]  sg_copy_from_iter+0x1f/0x40
[ 1352.412355]  copy_user_generic_unrolled+0x5d/0xd0
```

kernel-eng: preliminary read is pointing at a race in peer mapping (peer-to-peer dma map / unmap path). suspect SMMU/TLB invalidation ordering on the driver side when reloading modules.

matt: interesting — we saw similar symptoms last quarter but that was an older driver. What driver/kernel combos are these nodes on?

emma: nodes: ubuntu-22.04, kernel 5.15.0-1066, nvidia-driver 535.86.10 (modified build). All nodes hit are on a recent infra kernel-rollout that happened 2d ago.

pd-oncall: impact: ~10% of requests to hosted text-generation returned 500 in the last 10m, one high-value customer reported intermittent timeouts and got 2 5xx errors. Notified support and CS.

support: case #CS-4129 opened; customer-facing note drafted: "We are investigating intermittent GPU node restarts causing degraded availability for text generation; we will update in 30m."

raj: workaround idea: fallback route model-serving requests from Dedicated/hosted pool to CPU fallback instances for affected model routes, or switch to older model-version without the big conv kernels. Can we enable automatic fallback briefly?

emma: we can flip the routing policy for the affected model-route to use `fallback: cpu` in the console, but need an approvals gate. For immediate mitigation I'll update the route and run a canary.

incidentbot: Canary rollout initiated on route `text-gen-large` -> 5% CPU fallback. Observing latency.

ops-bot: Canary at 5% shows stable; error rate for canary 0.2%, serving runtime still fine on CPU.

kernel-eng: root cause hypothesis: concurrent unmap calls racing with active kernel launches after multi-GPU peer mapping changes. The misaligned address shows up when the device-side pointer references a stale mapping. This lines up with the kernel-rollout window.

sasha: recommend immediate next steps: 1) stop kernel rollouts (pause), 2) cordon other hit nodes (gpunode-21/24), 3) schedule full-driver rollback to prior build for a canary node, 4) keep draining affected nodes and route traffic off.

emma: pausing rollout now. cordoning gpunode-21 and gpunode-24.

ops-bot: rollout paused. gpunode-21 cordoned, gpunode-24 cordoned.

matt: can we repro on demand in staging with the exact driver/kernel combo? I'll spin a staging cluster and hammer with the same model to try to trigger the race. Need exact docker image and request pattern.

raj: sending a small repro harness to the kernel-eng DM with `--launch-concurrent=32 --seq-len=2048` pattern that previously tripped P2P races.

kernel-eng: running repro now in staging. If we reproduce, plan: 1) send minimal kernel patch ordering TLB invalidate after unmap, 2) backport to our driver package, 3) roll as hotpatch/rollback. If can't patch in time: roll driver back to previous GA build.

incidentbot: escalation to kernel-eng confirmed (priority-high). Expected initial RCA within 4h.

pd-oncall: handoff note for next shift: primary mitigations in place (nodes cordoned/draining, traffic partially routed to CPU fallback, rollout paused). Customer impact: limited but visible (10% error spike); support notified. Next oncall (lee) to monitor canary and driver rollback progress, own postmortem.

lee: I'll take the night handoff. logging handoff detail to the incident doc. Will coordinate with kernel-eng for rollback window.

support: CS update queued for 45m with timeline and mitigation steps.

emma: timeline summary: 00:00 alert, 00:02 cordon & drain gpunode-23, 00:08 detected driver/rollout correlation, 00:12 paused rollout, 00:18 canary CPU fallback enabled. Current status: stable canary, ongoing driver investigation.

raj: attaching small kernel oops grep and the minimal repro command here for visibility: `ssh staging && sudo ./repro --driver 535.86.10 --concurrent 32`.

matt: if kernel-eng confirms repro, prefer rollback driver to 535.78.05 for all affected host pools and then do a staged reintroduce of the newer driver after patch.

kernel-eng: agreed. prepping rollback artifact. will post checksum and instructions. ETA for first rollback canary: 90m.

incidentbot: NOTE: please add RCA owner to channel when assigned.

emma: assigning postmortem owner: raj. Raj will own RCA and timeline.

pd-oncall: closing tactical note: maintain channel, continue monitoring. Handoff to lee at 5201234589.

lee: acknowledged, will watch metrics/alerts and coordinate the rollback canary with kernel-eng.

support: will update CS-4129 when rollback canary completes.

incidentbot: Incident INC-2026-0431 updated: status -> 'mitigating', severity -> 'high', next-update -> 'in 30m'.

emma: quick follow-up: collect `nv-kernel.log` and `/var/log/syslog` from all cordoned nodes and upload to the incident storage bucket `s3://redwood-incidents/INC-2026-0431/` for later analysis.

raj: done. uploaded repro traces + core dumps. link: https://s3.console.aws.amazon.com/s3/object/redwood-incidents/INC-2026-0431/repro-traces.tar.gz

kernel-eng: thanks. I'll start looking at TLB invalidation paths and share a patch if we can.

emma: thx all. leaving channel open; handoff complete.
